chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who was on a journey with him, and with him was a slave girl and two slave boys. So he said to them both, 'You are both free for the sake of Allah, and testify that what is in the belly of this slave girl of mine is from me.' So she gave birth to a boy. When they returned to the heirs, they denied that and enslaved them. Then the two boys were emancipated after that, so they testified after being emancipated that their first master had testified that what was in the belly of his slave girl was from him.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their testimony is valid for the boy, and the boy whom they testified for cannot enslave them, because they affirmed his lineage.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the testimony of emancipated slaves regarding their master's declaration of paternity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the testimony of two emancipated slave boys regarding their master's declaration of paternity (Illa) for a child born to a slave girl, establishing that their proof of lineage prevents the child from enslaving them. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that emancipation and lineage confirmation are intrinsically linked, ensuring that the act of freeing slaves for God's sake secures their social and legal status within the family structure. The case underscores the importance of oral testimony in establishing nasab (lineage) in the absence of written documentation, a common scenario in early Islamic society.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Dawood Bin Abu Yazeed who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who was in a journey and with him was a slave girl of his, and two slave boys. So he said to them both, ‘You are both free for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I testify that whatever is in the belly of this slave girl of mine, is from me. So she gave birth to a boy. So when they proceeded to the inheritor, he denied that and enslaved them. Then the two slaves were emancipated after that, so they testified after having been emancipated that their master had at first testified that whatever was in the belly of his slave girl was from him’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Both their testimonies is allowed, and the boy whom they had testified for cannot enslave the two of them, because they had both affirmed his lineage’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Dawud ibn abu Yazid who has narrated the following: “

Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who on a journey was with a slave-girl and two slaves. He said to them, ‘You are free for the sake of Allah and bear witness that the child in the womb of the slave-girl is from me. She gave birth to a son. When they came back, the heir refused the will and kept them as slaves. The two slaves were later set free and they testified that their previous master had asked them to bear witness that the child in the womb of the slave-girl was his child.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Their testimony is acceptable and the child about whom they testified cannot make them slaves because they proved his genealogical relation.’”
